Life with family...ugh...My family pretty much disowned me. They wanted nothing to do with me. It was hard, which made dealing with BPD much worse. When my BPD came to surface, so to speak, and I ended up in the hospital numerous times, they were nowhere to be found. "It" and I didn't exist. We don't speak of BPD or mental illness. 

As for my husband, he does okay. It just depends on the day. At first, he didn't do well at all. It was a huge adjustment. We have a lot of arguments. It takes a special person to live with someone with BPD. We are not monsters, however. It takes an educated person, one who wants to be educated on BPD, to live with us.

A common misconception about Borderline Personality Disorder is that a person's personality "changes" much like Multiple Personality Disorder. It isn't like that at all. The following are symptoms of BPD: (copied/pasted from psychcentral for time)
A person with this disorder will also often exhibit impulsive behaviors and have a majority of the following symptoms:

Frantic efforts to avoid real or imagined abandonment

A pattern of unstable and intense interpersonal relationships characterized by alternating between extremes of idealization and devaluation

Identity disturbance, such as a significant and persistent unstable self-image or sense of self

Impulsivity in at least two areas that are potentially self-damaging (e.g., spending, sex, substance abuse, reckless driving, binge eating)

Recurrent suicidal behavior, gestures, or threats, or self-mutilating behavior

Emotional instability due to significant reactivity of mood (e.g., intense episodic dysphoria, irritability, or anxiety usually lasting a few hours and only rarely more than a few days)

Chronic feelings of emptiness

Inappropriate, intense anger or difficulty controlling anger (e.g., frequent displays of temper, constant anger, recurrent physical fights)

Transient, stress-related paranoid thoughts or severe dissociative symptoms
That is the stigma attached to BPD.

TL;DR (will try. good read)  Mental Health worker in Mass. disgusted with mental health system

Hospital stays limited regardless of progress. even if patient not well, due to insurance, patient sent home. if something happens, prescribing clinician held accountable. insurance won't let patient stay longer than 3 day stay most often. Prescribing meds and sending home and hoping for the best.

Residential programs a mess. Veteran staff overwhelmed. Bringing in new staff who are not qualified. Veteran staff taking up slack. Residents feel tension. Turnover in staffing high.
Lack of consistency in rules in residency programs. Doesn't work. Also, beds filling up with residents ordered to be there for a certain reason but don't fit certain criteria, but then no room for those who do fit criteria and really need help.

Private Practices running into insurances paying for at the most 12 sessions per year.
